aspect: EXAMPLE - 'doesn't transfer documents with the heading State of Palestine'
description: Gisha petitioned the Jerusalem District Court for a Gaza resident and her three children to travel to the West Bank to visit her husband, who was undergoing life-threatening surgery, after earlier requests were rejected without explanation. It was agreed Gisha would submit an official Palestinian Health Ministry medical document to COGAT - and the Israeli government then demanded it be routed via the Palestinian Civil Affairs Committee, saying it 'doesn't transfer documents with the heading State of Palestine'. Gisha published the insignia before and after redaction.
energy_note: A wife's hospital visit, held up by a logo.

aspect: The mechanism is that form is substitutable for substance
description: Nothing about the medical facts was in dispute. The objection was to two words in a header, and it worked, because a procedural objection does not have to be proportionate to function.
energy_note: An objection to typography, with medical consequences.

aspect: Which means no application is ever safely complete
description: If the letterhead can be the obstacle, then anything can be. There is no checklist that guarantees a submission is sufficient, so the applicant lives in permanent uncertainty about whether she has done enough.
energy_note: No way to know when your paperwork is finished.

aspect: It is also the whole conflict, compressed into a stationery dispute
description: The refusal to handle a paper bearing the words 'State of Palestine' is not incidental to the permit regime. It is the same position, expressed at the scale of one woman's hospital visit.
energy_note: The entire argument, printed at the top of a medical form.
